stem: Which statement is least consistent with good transition care for an adolescent with chronic disease?

options.text: Planning should start before transfer to adult services
The young person should be supported to build self-management skills
Care should simply be transferred to a specialist without involving the general practitioner
Parents and carers should be included appropriately while supporting autonomy
Written information and clear follow-up plans should be provided

explanation: Good transition care is planned, coordinated and developmentally appropriate, and usually includes primary care as well as paediatric and adult specialist teams. A simple handover to a specialist without coordination is not good transition care.
